### Purpose Statement

This standard defines mandatory requirements for installing, configuring, and deploying the Lenses.io Enterprise platform on AWS EKS as the centralized Kafka management and observability platform for the Enterprise Eventing as a Service (EaaS) initiative, as specified in [ADR-IFR-008](../../../decisions/infrastructure/ADR-IFR-008-kafka-management-platform-selection.md).

[standards/infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-001-platform-installation.md#scope]

### Scope

**In Scope**:
- Lenses.io Enterprise Edition deployment on AWS EKS
- Platform infrastructure provisioning (EKS cluster, RDS PostgreSQL, EBS storage)
- Helm chart configuration and deployment
- IAM authentication setup with IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts)
- Network configuration (VPC, security groups, ingress)
- Initial platform configuration and validation
- License management and activation

**Out of Scope**:
- MSK cluster registration (see STD-INFRA-KMGMT-002)
- RBAC and user access configuration (see STD-INFRA-KMGMT-003)
- SSO integration with Okta (see STD-INFRA-KMGMT-004)
- Specific feature configuration (monitoring, data lineage, etc.)

#### REQ-LENS-001-002: RDS PostgreSQL Database

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Lenses.io requires PostgreSQL for metadata storage

**Requirements**:
- Provision Amazon RDS PostgreSQL 14+ instance
- Use db.t3.medium instance minimum (2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM)
- Configure Multi-AZ deployment for HA
- Enable automated backups with 7-day retention
- Use encryption at rest with AWS KMS

**Implementation**:
```hcl
# RDS PostgreSQL for Lenses.io Metadata Storage
resource "aws_db_instance" "lenses_postgres" {
  identifier = "lenses-postgres-${var.environment}"

  # Engine configuration
  engine               = "postgres"
  engine_version       = "14.9"
  instance_class       = "db.t3.medium"
  allocated_storage    = 100
  max_allocated_storage = 500  # Enable storage autoscaling
  storage_type         = "gp3"
  storage_encrypted    = true
  kms_key_id          = aws_kms_key.rds.arn

  # Database configuration
  db_name  = "lenses"
  username = "lenses_admin"
  password = random_password.db_password.result
  port     = 5432

  # Multi-AZ for high availability
  multi_az               = true
  availability_zone      = null  # Auto-selected when multi_az = true

  # Network configuration
  db_subnet_group_name   = aws_db_subnet_group.lenses_postgres.name
  vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.rds_lenses.id]
  publicly_accessible    = false

  # Backup configuration
  backup_retention_period = 7
  backup_window          = "03:00-04:00"  # UTC
  maintenance_window     = "sun:04:00-sun:05:00"  # UTC

  # Snapshot configuration
  skip_final_snapshot       = false
  final_snapshot_identifier = "lenses-postgres-final-${var.environment}-${formatdate("YYYY-MM-DD-hhmm", timestamp())}"
  copy_tags_to_snapshot     = true

  # Monitoring and logging
  enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports = ["postgresql", "upgrade"]
  monitoring_interval             = 60
  monitoring_role_arn            = aws_iam_role.rds_monitoring.arn
  performance_insights_enabled    = true
  performance_insights_retention_period = 7
  performance_insights_kms_key_id = aws_kms_key.rds.arn

  # Auto minor version upgrade
  auto_minor_version_upgrade = true

  # Deletion protection
  deletion_protection = true

  # Parameter group
  parameter_group_name = aws_db_parameter_group.lenses_postgres.name

  # Option group
  option_group_name = aws_db_option_group.lenses_postgres.name

  tags = merge(var.common_tags, {
    Name      = "lenses-postgres-${var.environment}"
    Component = "lenses-database"
  })
}

# DB Subnet Group
resource "aws_db_subnet_group" "lenses_postgres" {
  name       = "lenses-postgres-subnet-${var.environment}"
  subnet_ids = var.database_subnet_ids

  tags = merge(var.common_tags, {
    Name = "lenses-postgres-subnet-group-${var.environment}"
  })
}

# DB Parameter Group
resource "aws_db_parameter_group" "lenses_postgres" {
  name   = "lenses-postgres-params-${var.environment}"
  family = "postgres14"

  # Performance tuning parameters
  parameter {
    name  = "shared_buffers"
    value = "4096000"  # 4GB in 8KB pages
  }

  parameter {
    name  = "effective_cache_size"
    value = "12288000"  # 12GB
  }

  parameter {
    name  = "maintenance_work_mem"
    value = "1048576"  # 1GB in KB
  }

  parameter {
    name  = "work_mem"
    value = "65536"  # 64MB in KB
  }

  parameter {
    name  = "max_connections"
    value = "200"
  }

  # Logging parameters
  parameter {
    name  = "log_statement"
    value = "ddl"
  }

  parameter {
    name  = "log_min_duration_statement"
    value = "1000"  # Log queries > 1 second
  }

  tags = var.common_tags
}

# DB Option Group
resource "aws_db_option_group" "lenses_postgres" {
  name                     = "lenses-postgres-options-${var.environment}"
  option_group_description = "Option group for Lenses.io PostgreSQL"
  engine_name              = "postgres"
  major_engine_version     = "14"

  tags = var.common_tags
}

# Security Group for RDS
resource "aws_security_group" "rds_lenses" {
  name_prefix = "lenses-rds-${var.environment}-"
  description = "Security group for Lenses.io RDS PostgreSQL"
  vpc_id      = var.vpc_id

  ingress {
    description     = "PostgreSQL from EKS nodes"
    from_port       = 5432
    to_port         = 5432
    protocol        = "tcp"
    security_groups = [module.lenses_eks_cluster.node_security_group_id]
  }

  egress {
    description = "Allow all outbound"
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 0
    protocol    = "-1"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }

  tags = merge(var.common_tags, {
    Name = "lenses-rds-sg-${var.environment}"
  })
}

# Random password for database
resource "random_password" "db_password" {
  length  = 32
  special = true
}

# Store password in AWS Secrets Manager
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "db_password" {
  name                    = "lenses-db-password-${var.environment}"
  description             = "PostgreSQL password for Lenses.io"
  recovery_window_in_days = 30
  kms_key_id             = aws_kms_key.secrets.arn

  tags = var.common_tags
}

resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "db_password" {
  secret_id = aws_secretsmanager_secret.db_password.id
  secret_string = jsonencode({
    username = aws_db_instance.lenses_postgres.username
    password = random_password.db_password.result
    engine   = "postgres"
    host     = aws_db_instance.lenses_postgres.address
    port     = aws_db_instance.lenses_postgres.port
    dbname   = aws_db_instance.lenses_postgres.db_name
  })
}

# KMS Key for RDS encryption
resource "aws_kms_key" "rds" {
  description             = "KMS key for Lenses.io RDS encryption"
  deletion_window_in_days = 30
  enable_key_rotation     = true

  tags = merge(var.common_tags, {
    Name = "lenses-rds-key-${var.environment}"
  })
}

resource "aws_kms_alias" "rds" {
  name          = "alias/lenses-rds-${var.environment}"
  target_key_id = aws_kms_key.rds.key_id
}

# IAM Role for RDS Enhanced Monitoring
resource "aws_iam_role" "rds_monitoring" {
  name = "lenses-rds-monitoring-${var.environment}"

  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [
      {
        Action = "sts:AssumeRole"
        Effect = "Allow"
        Principal = {
          Service = "monitoring.rds.amazonaws.com"
        }
      }
    ]
  })

  tags = var.common_tags
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "rds_monitoring" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.rds_monitoring.name
  policy_arn = "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonRDSEnhancedMonitoringRole"
}
```

#### REQ-LENS-001-004: Persistent Storage Configuration

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Lenses.io requires persistent storage for configuration and state

**Requirements**:
- Provision EBS gp3 volumes for Lenses.io pods
- Configure minimum 100 GB storage per pod
- Use StorageClass with reclaimPolicy: Retain
- Enable volume snapshots for backup
- Configure volume encryption with AWS KMS

**Implementation**:
```yaml
# StorageClass for Lenses.io Persistent Storage
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: lenses-gp3
  annotations:
    storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "false"
provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com
parameters:
  type: gp3
  iops: "3000"
  throughput: "125"
  encrypted: "true"
  kmsKeyId: ${KMS_KEY_ARN}
allowVolumeExpansion: true
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
reclaimPolicy: Retain

---
# PersistentVolumeClaim Template for Lenses Data
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: lenses-data-pvc
  namespace: lenses
  labels:
    app: lenses
    component: storage
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: lenses-gp3
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 100Gi

---
# PersistentVolumeClaim for Lenses Logs
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: lenses-logs-pvc
  namespace: lenses
  labels:
    app: lenses
    component: logs
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: lenses-gp3
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 50Gi

---
# VolumeSnapshot for Backup Configuration
apiVersion: snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: VolumeSnapshotClass
metadata:
  name: lenses-snapshot-class
  annotations:
    snapshot.storage.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "false"
driver: ebs.csi.aws.com
deletionPolicy: Retain
parameters:
  tagSpecification_1: "Name=lenses-snapshot"
  tagSpecification_2: "Environment=${ENVIRONMENT}"

---
# CronJob for Automated Snapshots
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: lenses-volume-snapshot
  namespace: lenses
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"  # Daily at 2 AM UTC
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 7
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: lenses-snapshot
          containers:
          - name: snapshot-creator
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -c
            - |
              cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
              apiVersion: snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1
              kind: VolumeSnapshot
              metadata:
                name: lenses-data-snapshot-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
                namespace: lenses
              spec:
                volumeSnapshotClassName: lenses-snapshot-class
                source:
                  persistentVolumeClaimName: lenses-data-pvc
              EOF
          restartPolicy: OnFailure

---
# ServiceAccount for Snapshot Operations
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: lenses-snapshot
  namespace: lenses

---
# Role for Snapshot Operations
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: lenses-snapshot-role
  namespace: lenses
rules:
- apiGroups: ["snapshot.storage.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["volumesnapshots"]
  verbs: ["create", "get", "list", "delete"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["persistentvolumeclaims"]
  verbs: ["get", "list"]

---
# RoleBinding for Snapshot ServiceAccount
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: lenses-snapshot-binding
  namespace: lenses
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: lenses-snapshot-role
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: lenses-snapshot
  namespace: lenses
```

```hcl
# Terraform configuration for EBS Snapshot Lifecycle
resource "aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy" "lenses_snapshots" {
  description        = "Lenses.io EBS snapshot lifecycle policy"
  execution_role_arn = aws_iam_role.dlm_lifecycle.arn
  state              = "ENABLED"

  policy_details {
    resource_types = ["VOLUME"]

    schedule {
      name = "Daily snapshots"

      create_rule {
        interval      = 24
        interval_unit = "HOURS"
        times         = ["03:00"]
      }

      retain_rule {
        count = 7
      }

      tags_to_add = {
        SnapshotCreator = "DLM"
        Environment     = var.environment
      }

      copy_tags = true
    }

    target_tags = {
      "kubernetes.io/created-for/pvc/name" = "lenses-data-pvc"
    }
  }

  tags = merge(var.common_tags, {
    Name = "lenses-snapshot-policy-${var.environment}"
  })
}

# IAM Role for DLM Lifecycle Policy
resource "aws_iam_role" "dlm_lifecycle" {
  name = "lenses-dlm-lifecycle-${var.environment}"

  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [
      {
        Action = "sts:AssumeRole"
        Effect = "Allow"
        Principal = {
          Service = "dlm.amazonaws.com"
        }
      }
    ]
  })

  tags = var.common_tags
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "dlm_lifecycle" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.dlm_lifecycle.name
  policy_arn = "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSDataLifecycleManagerServiceRole"
}
```

#### REQ-LENS-001-005: Helm Chart Deployment

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Official deployment method for Lenses.io

**Requirements**:
- Use Lenses.io official Helm chart version 5.0+
- Configure chart values via values.yaml (not inline)
- Store values.yaml in version control (Git)
- Use Helm secrets for sensitive values (license key, database password)
- Deploy to dedicated namespace: lenses-platform

**Implementation**:
```yaml
# Lenses.io Helm Chart Values (values.yaml)
lenses:
  # Database Configuration - PostgreSQL RDS
  storage:
    postgres:
      enabled: true
      host: ${RDS_ENDPOINT}
      port: 5432
      database: lenses
      username: lenses_admin
      # Password retrieved from AWS Secrets Manager
      passwordFromSecret:
        name: lenses-db-password
        key: password

  # Kafka Connection Configuration
  kafka:
    enabled: true
    bootstrapServers: ${MSK_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS}
    # IAM authentication for MSK
    sasl:
      mechanism: AWS_MSK_IAM
      awsMskIam:
        enabled: true
    # Enable TLS
    ssl:
      enabled: true
      truststore:
        type: JKS
    # Consumer/Producer configurations
    metrics:
      enabled: true
      port: 9102

  # Schema Registry Configuration (AWS Glue)
  schemaRegistries:
    enabled: true
    registries:
    - name: aws-glue
      type: AWS_GLUE
      urls:
      - "https://glue.${AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com"
      properties:
        region: ${AWS_REGION}
        # IAM role authentication via IRSA

  # Lenses Application Configuration
  lensesOpts: |
    -Xmx4g
    -Xms2g
    -XX:+UseG1GC
    -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200
    -Dlenses.security.mode=BASIC
    -Dlenses.secret.file=/mnt/secrets/security.conf

  # Security Configuration
  security:
    enabled: true
    # Admin user credentials from secret
    admin:
      usernameFromSecret:
        name: lenses-admin-creds
        key: username
      passwordFromSecret:
        name: lenses-admin-creds
        key: password
    # License from secret
    license:
      fromSecret:
        name: lenses-license
        key: license.json

  # Service Account with IRSA
  serviceAccount:
    create: true
    name: lenses
    annotations:
      eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: ${LENSES_IAM_ROLE_ARN}

  # Resource Limits and Requests
  resources:
    limits:
      cpu: 4000m
      memory: 8Gi
    requests:
      cpu: 2000m
      memory: 4Gi

  # Persistence Configuration
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    storageClass: lenses-gp3
    size: 100Gi
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce

  # Logging Configuration
  logging:
    level: INFO
    format: JSON
    destinations:
    - type: cloudwatch
      logGroup: /aws/lenses/${ENVIRONMENT}
      region: ${AWS_REGION}

  # High Availability Configuration
  replicaCount: 3

  podDisruptionBudget:
    enabled: true
    minAvailable: 2

  affinity:
    podAntiAffinity:
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 100
        podAffinityTerm:
          labelSelector:
            matchExpressions:
            - key: app
              operator: In
              values:
              - lenses
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
      - weight: 50
        podAffinityTerm:
          labelSelector:
            matchExpressions:
            - key: app
              operator: In
              values:
              - lenses
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone

  # Autoscaling Configuration
  autoscaling:
    enabled: true
    minReplicas: 3
    maxReplicas: 10
    targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 70
    targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage: 80

  # Health Checks
  livenessProbe:
    httpGet:
      path: /api/v1/health
      port: 3030
    initialDelaySeconds: 180
    periodSeconds: 30
    timeoutSeconds: 10
    successThreshold: 1
    failureThreshold: 3

  readinessProbe:
    httpGet:
      path: /api/v1/health/ready
      port: 3030
    initialDelaySeconds: 60
    periodSeconds: 10
    timeoutSeconds: 5
    successThreshold: 1
    failureThreshold: 3

  # Environment Variables
  env:
  - name: AWS_REGION
    value: ${AWS_REGION}
  - name: LENSES_OPTS
    value: |
      -Dlenses.kafka.topics.consumer.offsets=10000
      -Dlenses.kafka.topics.refresh=30000
      -Dlenses.jmx.port=9581

  # ConfigMap for additional configuration
  extraVolumes:
  - name: config
    configMap:
      name: lenses-config

  extraVolumeMounts:
  - name: config
    mountPath: /etc/lenses/config
    readOnly: true

# Monitoring Configuration
metrics:
  enabled: true
  serviceMonitor:
    enabled: true
    namespace: lenses
    interval: 30s
    scrapeTimeout: 10s
  prometheusRule:
    enabled: true
    rules:
    - alert: LensesPodDown
      expr: up{job="lenses"} == 0
      for: 5m
      labels:
        severity: critical
      annotations:
        summary: "Lenses pod is down"
        description: "Lenses pod {{ $labels.pod }} has been down for more than 5 minutes"
    - alert: LensesHighMemory
      expr: container_memory_usage_bytes{pod=~"lenses-.*"} / container_spec_memory_limit_bytes{pod=~"lenses-.*"} > 0.9
      for: 10m
      labels:
        severity: warning
      annotations:
        summary: "Lenses pod high memory usage"
        description: "Lenses pod {{ $labels.pod }} is using more than 90% of its memory limit"
```

```hcl
# Terraform Helm Release Configuration
resource "helm_release" "lenses" {
  name       = "lenses"
  repository = "https://lensesio.github.io/kafka-helm-charts"
  chart      = "lenses"
  version    = "5.5.0"  # Use latest stable version
  namespace  = kubernetes_namespace.lenses.metadata[0].name

  values = [
    templatefile("${path.module}/values.yaml", {
      RDS_ENDPOINT          = aws_db_instance.lenses_postgres.endpoint
      MSK_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS = var.msk_bootstrap_servers
      AWS_REGION            = var.aws_region
      ENVIRONMENT           = var.environment
      LENSES_IAM_ROLE_ARN   = aws_iam_role.lenses.arn
    })
  ]

  set_sensitive {
    name  = "lenses.storage.postgres.password"
    value = aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.db_password.secret_string
  }

  depends_on = [
    aws_db_instance.lenses_postgres,
    kubernetes_secret.lenses_license,
    kubernetes_secret.lenses_admin_creds,
    kubernetes_storage_class.lenses_gp3
  ]

  timeout = 600

  wait = true

  wait_for_jobs = true
}

# Kubernetes Namespace for Lenses
resource "kubernetes_namespace" "lenses" {
  metadata {
    name = "lenses"

    labels = {
      name        = "lenses"
      environment = var.environment
      managed-by  = "terraform"
    }
  }
}

# ConfigMap for Additional Configuration
resource "kubernetes_config_map" "lenses_config" {
  metadata {
    name      = "lenses-config"
    namespace = kubernetes_namespace.lenses.metadata[0].name
  }

  data = {
    "application.conf" = <<-EOT
      lenses {
        kafka {
          topics {
            max-partitions = 1000
            replication-factor = 3
          }
        }

        sql {
          execution-mode = IN_PROC
          state-store = PERSISTENT
        }

        alerts {
          enabled = true
          consumers {
            lag-threshold = 10000
          }
        }
      }
    EOT
  }
}
```

#### REQ-LENS-001-008: Initial Configuration Validation

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Ensure platform is operational before proceeding

**Requirements**:
- Verify all pods are in Running state
- Validate database connectivity
- Verify Lenses.io UI accessibility via ALB
- Test admin authentication with default credentials
- Verify Kubernetes health checks passing
- Document platform URLs and access methods

**Implementation**:
```bash
# Verify Pod Status
kubectl get pods -n lenses -o wide

# Expected output: All pods in Running state
# NAME                      READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
# lenses-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxx   1/1     Running   0          10m
# lenses-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxx   1/1     Running   0          10m
# lenses-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxx   1/1     Running   0          10m

# Check Pod Events
kubectl get events -n lenses --sort-by='.lastTimestamp'

# Verify Deployment Status
```

```yaml
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: lenses
  namespace: lenses
  labels:
    app: lenses
    prometheus: kube-prometheus
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: lenses
  endpoints:
  - port: metrics
    interval: 30s
    scrapeTimeout: 10s
    path: /metrics
    scheme: http
  namespaceSelector:
    matchNames:
    - lenses

# PrometheusRule for Lenses.io Alerts
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: lenses-alerts
  namespace: lenses
  labels:
    app: lenses
    prometheus: kube-prometheus
spec:
  groups:
  - name: lenses.rules
    interval: 30s
    rules:
    - alert: LensesPodDown
      expr: up{job="lenses", namespace="lenses"} == 0
      for: 5m
      labels:
        severity: critical
        component: lenses
      annotations:
        summary: "Lenses pod is down"
        description: "Lenses pod {{ $labels.pod }} in namespace {{ $labels.namespace }} has been down for more than 5 minutes"

    - alert: LensesHighMemoryUsage
      expr: |
        container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="lenses", pod=~"lenses-.*"}
        / container_spec_memory_limit_bytes{namespace="lenses", pod=~"lenses-.*"} > 0.9
      for: 10m
      labels:
        severity: warning
        component: lenses
      annotations:
        summary: "Lenses pod high memory usage"
        description: "Lenses pod {{ $labels.pod }} is using {{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of its memory limit"

    - alert: LensesHighCPUUsage
      expr: |
        rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="lenses", pod=~"lenses-.*"}[5m])
        / container_spec_cpu_quota{namespace="lenses", pod=~"lenses-.*"} > 0.8
      for: 10m
      labels:
        severity: warning
        component: lenses
      annotations:
        summary: "Lenses pod high CPU usage"
        description: "Lenses pod {{ $labels.pod }} is using {{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of its CPU limit"

    - alert: LensesPodRestartingFrequently
      expr: rate(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="lenses", pod=~"lenses-.*"}[1h]) > 0.1
      for: 5m
      labels:
        severity: warning
        component: lenses
      annotations:
        summary: "Lenses pod restarting frequently"
        description: "Lenses pod {{ $labels.pod }} has restarted {{ $value }} times in the last hour"

    - alert: LensesReplicasUnavailable
      expr: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="lenses", deployment="lenses"} < 2
      for: 5m
      labels:
        severity: critical
        component: lenses

        summary: "Lenses deployment has insufficient replicas"
```

# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview
This runbook provides step-by-step procedures for recovering the Lenses.io platform in case of disaster.

## Recovery Time Objective (RTO)
- Target: 4 hours
- Maximum acceptable downtime: 8 hours

## Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
- Target: 1 hour
- RDS automated backups: Point-in-time recovery available

## Prerequisites
- AWS CLI configured with appropriate credentials
- kubectl configured with cluster access
- Terraform state backup available
- Access to Git repository with IaC code

## Scenario 1: RDS Database Failure

### Detection
- CloudWatch alarm: RDS instance unreachable
- Lenses pods unable to connect to database

### Recovery Steps

1. **Identify latest backup**:
```bash
aws rds describe-db-snapshots \
  --db-instance-identifier lenses-postgres-${ENVIRONMENT} \
  --query 'reverse(sort_by(DBSnapshots, &SnapshotCreateTime))[0]'
```

2. **Restore from snapshot**:
```bash
aws rds restore-db-instance-from-db-snapshot \
  --db-instance-identifier lenses-postgres-${ENVIRONMENT}-restored \
  --db-snapshot-identifier <snapshot-id> \
  --db-subnet-group-name lenses-postgres-subnet-${ENVIRONMENT} \
  --vpc-security-group-ids <security-group-id> \
  --multi-az \
  --publicly-accessible false
```

3. **Update Terraform state** (if using Terraform):
```bash
terraform import aws_db_instance.lenses_postgres lenses-postgres-${ENVIRONMENT}-restored
```

4. **Update Helm values with new endpoint**:
```bash
NEW_ENDPOINT=$(aws rds describe-db-instances \
  --db-instance-identifier lenses-postgres-${ENVIRONMENT}-restored \
  --query 'DBInstances[0].Endpoint.Address' \
  --output text)

helm upgrade lenses lensesio/lenses \
  --namespace lenses \
  --set lenses.storage.postgres.host=${NEW_ENDPOINT} \
  --reuse-values
```

5. **Verify recovery**:
```bash
./validate-lenses.sh
```

#### Step 2: Configure Kubernetes Access

```bash
# Configure kubectl to access EKS cluster
aws eks update-kubeconfig \
  --region ${AWS_REGION} \
  --name ${EKS_CLUSTER_NAME}

# Verify cluster access
kubectl cluster-info
kubectl get nodes

# Create namespace (if not created by Terraform)

# Label namespace
kubectl label namespace lenses \
  environment=${ENVIRONMENT} \
  managed-by=terraform

# Create service account with IRSA annotation (if not created by Terraform)
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: lenses
  namespace: lenses
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: ${LENSES_IAM_ROLE}
EOF

```

#### Step 3: Create Secrets

```bash
# Create Lenses.io license secret
kubectl create secret generic lenses-license \
  --from-file=license.json=/path/to/lenses-license.json \
  --namespace=lenses

# Verify license secret
kubectl describe secret lenses-license -n lenses

# Create database password secret from AWS Secrets Manager
DB_PASSWORD=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
  --secret-id lenses-db-password-${ENVIRONMENT} \
  --query SecretString \
  --output text | jq -r .password)

kubectl create secret generic lenses-db-password \
  --from-literal=password="${DB_PASSWORD}" \
  --namespace=lenses

# Create admin credentials secret
ADMIN_USERNAME="admin"
ADMIN_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -base64 32)

kubectl create secret generic lenses-admin-creds \
  --from-literal=username="${ADMIN_USERNAME}" \
  --from-literal=password="${ADMIN_PASSWORD}" \
  --namespace=lenses

# Store admin password in AWS Secrets Manager for future reference
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name lenses-admin-password-${ENVIRONMENT} \
  --description "Lenses.io admin password" \
  --secret-string "{\"username\":\"${ADMIN_USERNAME}\",\"password\":\"${ADMIN_PASSWORD}\"}" \
  --region ${AWS_REGION}

# Verify all secrets
kubectl get secrets -n lenses

# Optional: Create TLS certificate secret (if not using ACM)
# kubectl create secret tls lenses-tls \
#   --cert=/path/to/tls.crt \
#   --key=/path/to/tls.key \
```

#### Step 4: Deploy Lenses.io via Helm

```bash
# Add Lenses.io Helm repository
helm repo add lensesio https://lensesio.github.io/kafka-helm-charts
helm repo update

# Search for available Lenses chart versions
helm search repo lensesio/lenses --versions

# Review Helm values file
cat helm/values.yaml

# Validate Helm chart with values
helm lint lensesio/lenses --values helm/values.yaml

# Perform dry-run to preview deployment
helm install lenses lensesio/lenses \
  --namespace lenses \
  --values helm/values.yaml \
  --dry-run \
  --debug > lenses-dry-run.yaml

# Review dry-run output
cat lenses-dry-run.yaml

# Deploy Lenses.io platform
helm install lenses lensesio/lenses \
  --namespace lenses \
  --values helm/values.yaml \
  --timeout 10m \
  --wait \
  --wait-for-jobs

# Monitor deployment progress
kubectl get pods -n lenses -w

# Check Helm release status
helm status lenses -n lenses

# View deployed resources
helm get manifest lenses -n lenses

# Verify deployment
kubectl get all -n lenses

# Check pod logs
kubectl logs -n lenses -l app=lenses --tail=100

# Verify ingress creation
kubectl get ingress -n lenses

# Get ALB URL
ALB_URL=$(kubectl get ingress lenses-ingress -n lenses \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].hostname}')

echo "Lenses platform deployed successfully!"
echo "Access URL: https://${LENSES_URL}"
echo "ALB DNS: ${ALB_URL}"
echo "Admin username: admin"
echo "Admin password: (stored in AWS Secrets Manager: lenses-admin-password-${ENVIRONMENT})"
```

#### Step 5: Validate Installation

```bash
# Run complete validation script (created in REQ-LENS-001-008)
./validate-lenses.sh

# Or run validation steps manually:

# 1. Check pod status
kubectl get pods -n lenses
kubectl describe pods -n lenses

# Verify all pods are Running
PODS_RUNNING=$(kubectl get pods -n lenses -l app=lenses \
  --field-selector=status.phase=Running \
  --no-headers | wc -l)

if [ ${PODS_RUNNING} -ge 3 ]; then
  echo "✓ All Lenses pods are running (${PODS_RUNNING} pods)"
else
  echo "✗ Expected at least 3 running pods, found ${PODS_RUNNING}"
  exit 1
fi

# 2. Check service endpoints
kubectl get svc -n lenses
kubectl describe svc lenses -n lenses

# Get service endpoint
SVC_ENDPOINT=$(kubectl get svc lenses -n lenses \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}')

echo "Service endpoint: ${SVC_ENDPOINT}"

# 3. Test health endpoint
LENSES_POD=$(kubectl get pods -n lenses -l app=lenses \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')

kubectl exec -n lenses ${LENSES_POD} -- \
  curl -s http://localhost:3030/api/v1/health

# 4. Test external access via ALB
curl -k -s https://${LENSES_URL}/api/v1/health

# Expected response: {"status":"healthy"}

# 5. Test admin login
RESPONSE=$(curl -k -s -X POST https://${LENSES_URL}/api/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{
    \"user\": \"admin\",
    \"password\": \"${ADMIN_PASSWORD}\"
  }")

if echo ${RESPONSE} | grep -q "token"; then
  echo "✓ Admin login successful"
else
  echo "✗ Admin login failed"
  echo "Response: ${RESPONSE}"
fi

# 6. Verify HPA and PDB
kubectl get hpa -n lenses
kubectl get pdb -n lenses

# 7. Check ingress and ALB
kubectl describe ingress lenses-ingress -n lenses

ALB_ARN=$(kubectl get ingress lenses-ingress -n lenses \
  -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.alb\.ingress\.kubernetes\.io/load-balancer-name}')

aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers \
  --names ${ALB_ARN} \
  --query 'LoadBalancers[0].State.Code' \
  --output text

# Expected: active

# 8. Verify database connectivity
kubectl exec -n lenses ${LENSES_POD} -- \
  psql -h ${RDS_ENDPOINT} \
       -U lenses_admin \
       -d lenses \
       -c "SELECT version();"

# 9. Check CloudWatch logs
aws logs tail /aws/lenses/${ENVIRONMENT} \
  --since 10m \
  --follow

# 10. Verify monitoring
kubectl get servicemonitor -n lenses
kubectl get prometheusrule -n lenses

echo ""
echo "=== Validation Complete ==="
echo "Lenses Platform URL: https://${LENSES_URL}"
echo "Admin Username: admin"
echo "Admin Password: (retrieve from AWS Secrets Manager)"
echo ""
echo "Next Steps:"
echo "1. Access Lenses UI and complete initial setup"
echo "2. Change admin password"
echo "3. Register Kafka clusters (see STD-INFRA-KMGMT-002)"
echo "4. Configure user access and permissions"
```

[standards/infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-001-platform-installation.md#helm-chart-upgrades]

#### Helm Chart Upgrades

```bash
# Helm Chart Upgrade Procedure

# 1. Check current version
helm list -n lenses

# 2. Update Helm repository
helm repo update

# 3. Check available versions
helm search repo lensesio/lenses --versions

# 4. Review release notes for target version
# Visit: https://docs.lenses.io/current/release-notes/

# 5. Backup current configuration
helm get values lenses -n lenses > lenses-values-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).yaml

# 6. Export current release manifest
kubectl get all -n lenses -o yaml > lenses-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).yaml

# 7. Create RDS snapshot before upgrade
aws rds create-db-snapshot \
  --db-instance-identifier lenses-postgres-${ENVIRONMENT} \
  --db-snapshot-identifier lenses-postgres-pre-upgrade-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

# 8. Test upgrade in staging environment first
# (Apply to staging, validate, then proceed to production)

# 9. Perform upgrade with updated values
helm upgrade lenses lensesio/lenses \
  --namespace lenses \
  --values helm/values.yaml \
  --version 5.6.0 \
  --timeout 10m \
  --wait \
  --atomic

# Note: --atomic flag will rollback automatically if upgrade fails

# 10. Monitor upgrade progress
kubectl rollout status deployment/lenses -n lenses
kubectl get pods -n lenses -w

# 11. Validate upgraded platform
./validate-lenses.sh

# 12. Test critical functionality
curl -k https://${LENSES_URL}/api/v1/health
curl -k https://${LENSES_URL}/api/v1/license

# 13. Check Helm release history
helm history lenses -n lenses

# Rollback Procedure (if needed)

# 1. Check release history
helm history lenses -n lenses

# Output example:
# REVISION  UPDATED                   STATUS      CHART          APP VERSION  DESCRIPTION
# 1         Mon Jan 15 10:00:00 2024  superseded  lenses-5.5.0   5.5.0        Install complete
# 2         Mon Feb 10 15:30:00 2024  deployed    lenses-5.6.0   5.6.0        Upgrade complete

# 2. Rollback to previous revision
helm rollback lenses -n lenses

# Or rollback to specific revision
helm rollback lenses 1 -n lenses

# 3. Monitor rollback
kubectl rollout status deployment/lenses -n lenses

# 4. Validate after rollback
./validate-lenses.sh

# 5. If rollback fails, restore from backup
kubectl delete all -n lenses --all
kubectl apply -f lenses-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).yaml

# Version Compatibility Checks

# Before upgrading, verify:
# 1. Kubernetes version compatibility
KUBE_VERSION=$(kubectl version --short | grep Server | awk '{print $3}')
echo "Kubernetes version: ${KUBE_VERSION}"
# Lenses 5.6+ requires Kubernetes 1.23+

# 2. PostgreSQL version compatibility
PG_VERSION=$(kubectl exec -n lenses deployment/lenses -- \
  psql -h ${RDS_ENDPOINT} -U lenses_admin -d lenses \
  -t -c "SELECT version();" | grep PostgreSQL)
echo "PostgreSQL version: ${PG_VERSION}"
# Lenses 5.x requires PostgreSQL 12+

# 3. Helm version
helm version --short
# Requires Helm 3.8+

# 4. Check for breaking changes in release notes
# Review: https://docs.lenses.io/current/release-notes/breaking-changes/

# 5. Verify license compatibility
kubectl exec -n lenses deployment/lenses -- \
  curl -s http://localhost:3030/api/v1/license | jq .

# Post-Upgrade Tasks

# 1. Update documentation with new version
echo "Lenses.io version: 5.6.0" >> deployment-log.txt

# 2. Notify stakeholders
aws sns publish \
  --topic-arn ${SNS_TOPIC_ARN} \
  --subject "Lenses.io Platform Upgraded" \
  --message "Lenses.io has been successfully upgraded to version 5.6.0 in ${ENVIRONMENT} environment."

# 3. Update monitoring dashboards if needed

# 4. Schedule post-upgrade review meeting
```
